title: Bind declared artifacts and state to the attempt before execution
observations: The retrospective separates attempt-specific runtime records from current-run evidence, and warns against treating a prior run or retrospective as current-run evidence.
The offline preflight tooling, not the retrospective, defines declared package and capture binding to an attempt.
interpretation: Check declared artifact, attempt and expected boot bindings with the offline preflight before proposing execution.
counterevidence: Matching local declarations and digests do not establish live state or authorization.
An offline binding check is not evidence of a current hardware run.
unresolved_questions: Are current artifacts, boot identity and prerequisite state independently verified?

source_references.summary: Retrospective separation of attempt-specific runtime records from current-run evidence.
Preflight tooling defines declared package and capture binding; not a retrospective finding.
